base_record_snapshot.lesson:
The t611 reader-side divergence cure gives marker vocabulary for exactly TWO loci — the
queue row and its source file — but the append-only-never-retcon law GUARANTEES that a
correction is appended where it happened, which is structurally often a THIRD surface
(e.g. a record_correction row in a reviews ledger) that is neither of the two. When the
row and its source file agree with each other, no divergence marker can fire — the
agreement itself is the trap (Disagreement-as-evidence, inverted: two surfaces agree on
evidence a third surface has disproven). The docket reader then inherits a disproven
evidence claim with zero signal. This recurs BY DESIGN, not incidentally: every
never-retcon correction to an already-extracted claim lands outside the row/source pair.
Candidate cure (named at stepper 661, NOT built): a typed correction back-reference — the
correcting row names the corrected queue id — resolved by a deterministic reconciler pass
that mints the reader-side staleness marker on the affected row; the author bodies stay
untouched (t611). Until then, third-surface corrections are only found by hand-probing,
which is exactly the un-wired-rehydration failure mode (Case 2).
